findings.reason: The approved batch page manifest requires randomized-quasi-monte-carlo-and-replicates, but the current A page omits it. The assigned dyadic-projection lemma uses lem-b-adic-step-functions-dense-in-l2-cube, which is housed on that page. Add the missing page requirement.
The Definition uses the polar surface measure and well-definedness results whose stated hypotheses include Countable Choice, but does not state that premise. Make Countable Choice explicit.
The proof uses the Countable-Choice hypotheses of the polar-coordinate, completed-product Tonelli, and countable-null-set suppliers, while its Statement omits Countable Choice.
Its proof uses completed-product Tonelli/Fubini under Countable Choice, as its axiom-use note also acknowledges, but the Statement does not state that hypothesis.
The surface-measure convention it uses is defined under Countable Choice. State the inherited premise in the Statement.
Step 1.2 writes the phase bound with commas between |k|, |y|, and |theta-theta'|; state their product explicitly.

The proof uses thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure, whose Statement requires Countable Choice. It also applies a density result for Borel-cube L2 to a zero extension measurable for the completed Lebesgue measure without supplying a Borel representative. State the choice premise and justify that transfer, for example through the completed-measurable representative result.
The Definition uses the dyadic projection and model/operator interfaces whose required Countable Choice premise is omitted. State the inherited hypothesis.

The Definition introduces f only in f_N=P_N f without specifying f in L2(D). Its cell-pair formula also equates an inner product with a double integral without making the Fubini/absolute-integrability use explicit.

The polar surface measure definition requires Countable Choice, and the stated well-definedness supplier for the normalized Legendre polynomial assumes Countable and Dependent Choice. State these premises or separate the choice-free definitional claims.
The polar-coordinate, second-Green, completed-product Fubini, and locally-integrable-distribution suppliers used in the proof require Countable Choice, but the Statement omits it.
The example claims Born solvability and error using a theorem that assumes Countable Choice; neither the Example nor its Given clause states that premise.
Steps 2.1 and 3.1 apply the norm-limit-of-compact-operators theorem to L2(D), whose Banach-space hypothesis is not established. Under the stated AC, cite and use the L2-completeness supplier.

In step 1.2 the Schur column bound takes a supremum over every y although q is only an L-infinity equivalence class; choose an everywhere bounded representative or use an almost-everywhere Schur bound. Step 1.3 also needs the finite-product argument that combines compact real- and imaginary-part closures into compactness in complex C.

Step 2.1 shows the operator-image union is totally bounded, then invokes compactness of its closure without showing that the closure remains totally bounded and complete. Add those steps or the precise suppliers. State f and u in L2(D) explicitly.

Step 2.3 says rotations act unitarily on H_l and uses rotational invariance to make Z_l(omega,omega) constant, but does not establish rotation invariance of the defined polar surface measure. Supply the determinant-one change-of-variables argument and invariance of harmonic restrictions.

The Statement says to write each incident mode as alpha_lm r j_l(kr), but assumes only a classical free Helmholtz field and the proof never derives that regular-origin form. Specify regularity/domain at the origin and derive it from the radial equation, or state the mode form as an explicit hypothesis.
